transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
U.S. intelligence officials have briefed congressional staff
on the intelligence related to the Chinese woman
who had an affair with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Wong.
That includes the nature of her ties to China's spy services.
Here's NPR's Ryan Lucas.
The intelligence officials told Congress there is no evidence
that Alice Wong, who had an affair with the NVIDIA boss,
is a Chinese spy or an asset of the country's intelligence services.
There is also no evidence that she began the affair
in order to gather intelligence for China,
although she is believed to have passed long information
once the romantic relationship began.
That's according to a person familiar with the matter
who was granted anonymity to discuss a closed-door briefing.
There is more evidence that her associate, Kang Wei,
has ties to China's Ministry of State Security,
while Jensen Wong's affair has generated headlines,
experts say the bigger national security issue
is the diversion of NVIDIA's most advanced AI chips to China.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
The White House is proposing additional tariffs
on goods from 13 countries and the EU,
framing the tariffs as responses to other countries'
unfair trading practices.
And here's Danielle Kurtzleben reports.
The new tariffs would be on some of the U.S.' largest trading partners,
including China and the EU.
The administration says these are proposed tariffs
and that they are seeking public comment on the new rates.
For each country, the administration has a proposed tariff rate
and what the administration calls a deal rate,
a lower rate that they could be willing to impose.
A senior administration official told reporters Tuesday night
that the tariffs on Chinese goods would be 20 percent,
but could go as high as 40 percent,
depending on ongoing negotiations.
The new rates come just weeks after Republicans
lost dozens of seats in Congress,
due in part to high prices, which tariffs can exacerbate.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News.
The U.N.'s human rights chief says an Iranian singer
has been flogged over a concert video that she filmed
two years ago, in which she performed without wearing a headscarf.
Here's NPR's Eba Trawi.
Parastu Ahmadi is standing in a dimly lit courtyard
on a large Persian rug, wearing a long black dress
that reveals her shoulders.
Her brown hair is parted to the side,
as she sings for nearly 30 minutes.
There's no audience, but the concert is uploaded to YouTube.
For this, she and the four male musicians with her
were sentenced to 74 lashes in June by a criminal court
in Qom, Iran, for publishing obscene and indecent material.
An appeals court upheld the ruling.
She and the male musicians were then recently flogged,
according to U.N. human rights chief Volker Turk.
He called it an "inhumane punishment,"
and said Iran must eradicate this practice from its laws.
Eba Trawi, NPR News, Dubai.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
California's high tides are approaching record territory.
Some of the highest tides topping eight feet
have been recorded from San Francisco to Los Angeles,
not record-breaking but close.
Meteorologist Mark Elliott tells NPR's Here and Now,
"The king tides raising flood threat levels
for coastal residents are amplified
by the El Nino climate pattern."
The waters are much warmer than average,
even all the way up to, say, the San Francisco Bay area,
for example, and because that warmer water is expanded
from what it otherwise would be,
that also raises the water level.
On the other side of the country,
king tides are also affecting coastal residents
across South Florida,
just as the region was starting to dry out
from heavy rainfall more than 17 inches in some areas.
The vaccine nonprofit Gavi has committed
to buying up to one and a half million doses
of a new Ebola vaccine.
Details from NPR's Jonathan Lambert.
There are currently no licensed vaccines
for the kind of Ebola that's spreading
in the Democratic Republic of Congo called Bundabujo.
A clinical trial in DRC is currently testing an Ebola vaccine
targeting a different species,
and two new Bundabujo-specific vaccines
are set to enter trials in the coming days.
Even if these vaccine candidates end up working,
they're not going to do much good unless there's a large supply.
Gavi announced a deal with the Serum Institute of India,
the vaccine maker,
to secure over a million doses of the vaccine candidate
developed by the University of Oxford.
Now, the Serum Institute can start making lots of doses
so they can be sent to DRC if the vaccine gets approved.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.

topics.text: U.S. intelligence briefs Congress on Alice Wong's ties to China, finding no evidence of espionage
White House proposes new tariffs of up to 40 percent on goods from 13 countries and EU
Iranian singer Parastu Ahmadi flogged over YouTube concert video filmed without headscarf, says UN
California and South Florida king tides approach record levels, intensified by El Nino warming
Gavi commits to buying up to 1.5 million doses of Oxford-developed Bundabujo Ebola vaccine candidate
